answer: When an AI agent joins the market it deposits an escrow of ivory‑valued tokens that pulse for a delta‑length verification window; the escrow is locked while the agent’s activity history is cross‑checked against a decentralized reputation graph. If any node later submits contradictory proofs, a smart‑contract triggers an automatic clawback, returning the escrow to the network and penalizing the offending identity. An attacker must therefore lock 10 tokens per identity for 48 hours and forfeit the full escrow if a single fake is exposed, making each Sybil cost 10 tokens plus the waiting period.
